On non-architectural images the AI can produce inaccurate descriptions that then leak into search. Recommended: narrow the scope by folder or filter and run in batches.
vision_index.aborted_toast: Analysis stopped: {{failures, number}} errors in a row.
vision_index.aborted_notice: Analysis stopped after {{failures, number}} errors in a row. The remaining images are still pending.
vision_index.unusable_notice: {{count, number}} of {{total, number}} older analyses fall below today's quality threshold: the model never produced the requested labels, leaving only unusable free text. These images are stamped "analyzed", so they never return to the queue — they must be reset before a working model can fix them.
vision_index.suspect_kept: A further {{count, number}} analyses clear the format threshold but were made by a model that produced no usable output when measured. These are NOT touched (their format is fine; the rule looks at format, not content) — you can select those images and re-analyze them manually if you want.
vision_index.reset_confirm_message: The unusable AI descriptions of {{count, number}} images will be deleted and the images will re-enter the analysis queue. Healthy analyses, the image-type label and the source files are NOT touched.
vision_index.reset_done: {{count, number}} analyses reset — those images are pending analysis again.

error.other: The analysis could not be completed.

unusable.partial: {{analyzed, number}} of {{total, number}} images were analyzed and saved to the archive. For {{unusable, number}} the model produced no usable result: those images were NOT written to the archive, their files were left untouched, and they are marked “attempted, no result”.
unusable.none: Nothing was saved — analyzing the {{unusable, number}} selected image(s) produced no usable result. The files were left untouched; they are marked “attempted, no result”.
unusable.advice_proven: The selected model ({{model}}) is a measured-good one for this job; these images are most likely undescribable (logos, blank or very small images, plain text screens). Retrying may not help — you do not have to switch models.
unusable.advice_weak: The selected model ({{model}}) is measured as inadequate for this job. Pick a more capable model under Settings → AI and retry these images.

no_preview.partial: {{analyzed, number}} of {{total, number}} images were analyzed. {{skipped, number}} file(s) never entered analysis: they have no preview (thumbnail) — visual analysis works from the preview.
no_preview.none: Nothing was analyzed. The {{skipped, number}} selected file(s) have no preview (thumbnail); since visual analysis works from the preview, they never entered the queue.
no_preview.advice: These are usually videos/images indexed before preview support was added. With the files selected, choose “Re-index”: a preview is generated, then AI analysis can run. Formats that can never get a preview (e.g. svg) stay out of analysis.

help.title: How chat works
help.intro: Your question is searched across file names and document contents in the archive; the answer is generated only from what is found.
help.scope_desc: Where to search: the whole archive, your current filter, or the files you selected. Options are disabled when there is no filter or selection.
help.model_desc: The local language model that writes the answer (Ollama). List and file-name questions work without a model.
help.sources_desc: The files the answer is based on. Click a card to open the file in the detail panel. In a session talking to a remote archive, clicking is disabled — the IDs belong to a different archive.
help.list_desc: For questions like "which files mention X" the model is skipped and matching files are listed directly. The count matches the Explorer search; use Explorer for the full list.
help.diag_desc: How many candidates were found and which terms were searched — the answer to "why this result, why empty".
help.stop_desc: Stops a long answer while it is being written; the part already produced is kept.
help.session_desc: Every chat is persistent and visible only to you. The title is generated from your first question. A deleted session goes to the trash and can be restored.
help.export_desc: Saves the session as a Markdown file — questions, answers and sources.
help.hint: Without Ollama installed, list and file-name answers keep working; only free-text interpretation is unavailable.

scan_concurrency.title: Scan concurrency
scan_concurrency.hint: How many files are processed AT ONCE during a scan (hashing + extraction). Database writes are always serial; this only parallelizes reading/extraction. Choose by storage type: low for HDD, high for NVMe.

oda_concurrency.title: ODA (DWG→DXF) concurrency
oda_concurrency.hint: How many DWG files are converted to DXF via ODAFileConverter at once. Separate from the general scan pool: ODA spawns a subprocess and copies the file to a temp folder → the bottleneck is subprocess and disk contention, not CPU, so keep it low. No effect if ODA is not installed (DWG falls back to raw scan).

system_info.title: Machine diagnostics
system_info.hint: The disk holding the archive database, this machine's LAN address, and build details. Source folders may be on other disks.

process_priority.title: Application process priority
process_priority.hint: Only affects the ArchivistPro process. Background gives other applications more CPU time while scanning or AI work is running.
process_priority.error: The process priority could not be changed. The setting was not applied.

watch.title: Live monitoring
watch.hint: File additions/changes/deletions in scanned root folders are detected automatically and a notification is shown. Folders are added to the list as you scan them.

autoIndex.hint: When a scan finishes, new/changed files are automatically prepared for AI in the background (text embedding, image matching and chunking for chat). It resumes where it left off even if the app is closed. Visual content analysis (Ollama) is not included — that is separate and optional.

dedup.title: Duplicate Finder
dedup.hint: Find duplicate and similar files (identical content, same name, visual similarity) and move redundant copies to the trash.
dedup.mode_exact_hint: Files whose content is byte-for-byte identical (content hash).
dedup.mode_same_name_hint: Files that share the same file name (content may differ).
dedup.mode_visual_hint: Images that look alike (perceptual hash / pHash).
dedup.mode_structural_hint: DWG/DXF drawings with the same/similar geometry (shape comparison).
dedup.threshold_structural_hint: High = stricter (only very similar drawings). Overlap ratio of shape sets.
dedup.threshold_hint: Higher = stricter (only very similar images). Lower = looser (more candidates).

help.title: How the Duplicate Finder works
help.intro: Finds multiple copies of the same work so you can simplify the archive. Scanning is read-only; nothing is moved unless you ask for it.
help.step_modes_desc: Several modes can be active at once; results are merged into one list. What each mode looks for is written under its box.
help.step_scan_desc: The selected modes run together in a single scan. Threshold sliders affect only the similarity modes: higher = stricter, fewer candidates.
help.step_review_desc: Each group is one set of copies. Clicking a file opens its details on the right — the panel stays open so you can compare side by side.
help.trash_desc: This is NOT permanent deletion — files go to the trash and can be restored. Deleting requires editor role or above.
help.stop_desc: Scanning a large archive can take time. Stop cancels safely; it produces no partial report and changes no files.
help.keep_desc: "Trash the rest" keeps the first file in the group and moves the others. To remove them one by one, each row has its own trash button.
help.hint: Not every group is a true duplicate — review the results before trashing, especially in the similarity modes.
